name: The Roman world
blurb: Sentences about the state, the army, the home, the gods, nature, the mind, travel and time, using the words that turn up most in Latin writing. Opens after “Belonging and giving”.

units.title: State and law
units.intro: The Roman state ran on magistrates, law and the people’s say. Words for rule and justice, in sentences you can already build: the consuls rule, the judge hears the case, nobody is greater than the law.

units.title: The army
units.intro: Rome grew by its legions. Soldiers, camps, spears and standards. Note _castra_: it looks plural but means one camp.

units.title: Family and home
units.intro: The household (_familia_) was the Roman world in small. Parents, children, the lady of the house, the heir.

units.title: Gods and fate
units.intro: Romans lived with their gods and with fate. _deus_ is irregular in the plural (_dī_ or _deī_, genitive _deōrum_), and _dea_ has its own dative and ablative plural, _deābus_.

units.title: Nature
units.intro: Wind, fire, trees and rivers. Comparison comes back: the sun is bigger _than the moon_, with the ablative.

units.title: Mind and speech
units.intro: How Romans talked about thinking and saying. _vīs_ (force) is irregular: _vim_, _vī_.

units.title: Travel
units.intro: Roads, ships, harbors and provinces. “To” a town is just the accusative: _Rōmam_.

units.title: Time
units.intro: Days, years, nights and hours. How long takes the accusative (_multōs diēs_); when takes the ablative (_nocte_, _hieme_).
